description: Architecture decision constraint sheet and decision record format.
default_posture: Prefer modular application with clear internal boundaries and managed identity/data services. Independent services only when measured scaling, isolation, ownership, or release needs warrant them.

dimensions.name: coupling
dimensions.note: fan_in = who depends on this. fan_out = what this depends on. blast_radius = if this breaks, what else breaks. stability = settled vs actively changing. module_depth = Ousterhout's deep-module ratio (interface width vs implementation depth).

dimensions.name: migration
dimensions.rule: Every non-trivial change to existing code requires a transition strategy. 'Deploy and hope' is not a plan.

dimensions.name: observability
dimensions.rule: Specify how you will KNOW this works in production, not just that it works in dev. For each external connector (Azure, AWS, Linear, PostHog, etc.): credential location, SLA, cost model, failure mode, monitoring endpoint.

dimensions.name: reversibility

examples.trivial: Config change, feature flag toggle, UI copy
examples.expensive: Schema migration, API version, dependency upgrade
examples.irreversible: Data deletion, public API contract, external integration go-live

dimensions.rule: Analysis depth scales with irreversibility. A trivial change does not need a full constraint sheet. An irreversible change needs every dimension filled.

dimensions.name: ownership
dimensions.rule: Conway's Law is real. A decision requiring daily cross-team coordination has different cost than one that doesn't. Name the teams, not just the code.

dimensions.name: alternatives
dimensions.rule: At most two credible alternatives. Document why the default fails or remains adequate.

dimensions.name: revisit_trigger
dimensions.rule: An observable condition that would invalidate the decision. Example: sustained queue latency exceeding agreed SLO.

stopping_criteria: Recommendation is reversible or has reviewed migration plan
stopping_rule: Research only concrete decisions whose answer could change the implementation.

principles.principle: Design > Functionality > Complexity > Tests. Solve the problem you know needs solving now.
Lightweight embedded specification in the code rather than separate formal system.

exemplars.pattern: Single schema.json is source of truth for field names, types, max lengths, PK, defaults. Codegen produces dataclasses. No hand-written model can drift from the database.
UoW owns connection, cursor, commit/rollback boundary. Savepoints for partial-batch rollback. Teardown asymmetric: commit failures propagate, rollback/close failures swallowed.
100+ read routes declared as frozen dataclasses, validated at import time. Unknown tables, unknown columns, mismatched route params all fail before any request.
demonstrates: default_posture (modular app with clear internal boundaries)
